name: TAb show cam is on
description:
1. Fixed the Meet panel tab missing its camera icon by adding a global, meet-independent `localCameraEnabled` flag to the `meets` store that `MeetView` publishes on camera start/stop, which `Tab.vue` reads — so the icon shows even in the pre-join lobby where no meet exists.
2. Extended the same pattern to the microphone: added `localMicEnabled`/`micLevel` state plus `isLocalMicOn`/`isMicSpeaking` getters to the store, fed by a new Web Audio monitor (`src/utils/audioLevel.js`) that publishes a 0–100 input level.
3. Created a shared `MicIndicator.vue` component that shows a mic/mic-slash icon and a green pulse ring while the mic is unmuted AND audio is detected, reused in the Tab, Meet lobby, call controls, and participant list.
4. After `meets.js` and `MeetView.vue` were changed by other work, reviewed and re-applied the mic state (store) and mic wiring (MeetView imports, `micMonitor`, `enableMic`/`disableMic`) while preserving the new `joinMeet`/`storeCurrentMeetId` behavior.
5. Net result: one reusable mic indicator used everywhere, pulsing when you actually speak, with the camera icon behavior intact and accessible `aria-label`s throughout.

evaluateChangeRisk() {
      const { deletions, insertions } = this.parseStatsString()
      const originalLines = this.orgContent?.split('\n').length || 1
      const newLines = this.effectiveCode?.split('\n').length || 1
      const deletionRatio = deletions / originalLines
      const lineChangeRatio = Math.abs(newLines - originalLines) / originalLines
      const totalChanges = deletions + insertions
      const changeIntensity = totalChanges / originalLines
      const DANGEROUS_DELETION_RATIO = 0.4
      const DANGEROUS_INTENSITY = 0.5
      const DANGEROUS_LINE_LOSS = 0.3
      const isDeletion = deletionRatio > DANGEROUS_DELETION_RATIO
      const isHighIntensity = changeIntensity > DANGEROUS_INTENSITY
      const isLineLoss = lineChangeRatio > DANGEROUS_LINE_LOSS && deletions > insertions
      this.isDangerousChange = isDeletion || isHighIntensity || isLineLoss
      this.changeRiskMessage = this.generateRiskMessage(deletionRatio, changeIntensity, lineChangeRatio, deletions, insertions)

history.summary:
1. **Request:** Show a cam icon on the Meet tab whenever the user's camera is on.
2. **Discovery:** The meets store (`src/store/meets.js`) already exposes reactive `activeMeets[meetId].localStream`, containing a video track only while the camera is enabled.
3. **Approach:** Reuse that existing state — no store changes needed; work was scoped to `src/components/desktop/Tab.vue` only.
4. **Implementation:** Added computeds `isMeet`, `meetId`, `cameraOn`, and `showCameraIcon`, plus a conditional `<i class="fa-solid fa-video text-success">` icon in the tab name row.
5. **Result:** The camera icon renders only for Meet tabs with an active camera, with `title`/`aria-label` included for accessibility.

The user asked to display a camera icon on the Meet tab whenever the local camera is on.
The first attempt derived "camera on" only from the meet's store-published local stream.
This failed on the pre-join lobby, where no active meet exists, so no stream is published to the store.
The fix added a global `localCameraEnabled` flag in the meets store, set/cleared by MeetView's camera start/stop.
Tab.vue now reads that flag (with stream fallback), so the cam icon shows in both the lobby and active calls.

1. Fixed the Meet tab's missing camera icon by promoting the local camera state to a global, meet-independent flag in the `meets` store, so it works even in the pre-join lobby where no meet is active.
2. `MeetView` now publishes camera on/off to the store via `setLocalCameraEnabled`, and `Tab.vue` reads it (falling back to the active meet's stream).
3. Extended the same pattern to the microphone: added global `localMicEnabled` + `micLevel` state (with `isLocalMicOn`/`isMicSpeaking` getters) to the `meets` store.
4. Created a reusable `MicIndicator` component (mic/slashed-mic icon with a green pulse ring while speaking) plus a `audioLevel.js` Web Audio helper that analyzes the mic stream and reports a 0–100 level.
5. Wired `MicIndicator` everywhere — the desktop Tab, Meet lobby and in-call controls, and the participants list — so the mic state is consistent across the UI, with `aria-label` accessibility support.

1. Fixed the Meet panel tab missing its camera icon by adding a global, meet-independent `localCameraEnabled` flag to the `meets` store that `MeetView` publishes on camera start/stop, which `Tab.vue` reads — so the icon shows even in the pre-join lobby where no meet exists.
2. Extended the same pattern to the microphone: added `localMicEnabled`/`micLevel` state plus `isLocalMicOn`/`isMicSpeaking` getters to the store, fed by a new Web Audio monitor (`src/utils/audioLevel.js`) that publishes a 0–100 input level.
3. Created a shared `MicIndicator.vue` component that shows a mic/mic-slash icon and a green pulse ring while the mic is unmuted AND audio is detected, reused in the Tab, Meet lobby, call controls, and participant list.
4. After `meets.js` and `MeetView.vue` were changed by other work, reviewed and re-applied the mic state (store) and mic wiring (MeetView imports, `micMonitor`, `enableMic`/`disableMic`) while preserving the new `joinMeet`/`storeCurrentMeetId` behavior.
5. Net result: one reusable mic indicator used everywhere, pulsing when you actually speak, with the camera icon behavior intact and accessible `aria-label`s throughout.
